questions.question: How do you build responsive layouts — media queries, breakpoints, and mobile-first?
questions.title: Responsive Media Queries
questions.direct_answer: Mobile-first: write the base styles for the smallest screen, then use min-width media queries to layer complexity as screens grow. Breakpoints chosen by CONTENT behavior (where the layout breaks), not device sizes — though common anchors are ~480/768/1024px. Modern additions reduce query dependence: relative units (rem, %, clamp()), flexible grids, auto-fit/minmax Grid, container queries (respond to the component's container, not the viewport), and fluid typography via clamp().

Mental Model

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    M[base styles: mobile] --> Q1{min-width 48em?}
    Q1 -->|yes| T[tablet: 2-col grid]
    T --> Q2{min-width 75em?}
    Q2 -->|yes| D[desktop: 3-col, more padding]
    A[auto-fit + minmax] -.no queries.-> F[columns adapt purely by space]
    C[container queries] -.component-level.-> CC[card adapts to its own box]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The viewport meta (the prerequisite people forget): `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` makes the browser lay out at the device's real width instead of a virtual 980px — without it, media queries fire against the virtual viewport and your responsive CSS does nothing on phones. This is the classic 'works on desktop resize, broken on the actual phone' bug.

Container queries (the 2023+ shift worth naming): viewport queries made COMPONENTS that look different at the same viewport width — a card in a wide main column vs the same card in a narrow sidebar. @container responds to the nearest container-type: inline-size ancestor: the card layout adapts to ITS box, wherever it's placed. The consequence: truly reusable components whose layout depends on their context, not the page — the modular-CSS goal viewport queries could never deliver.

The testing realities (the practical close): verify at real breakpoints (DevTools device mode), test the awkward widths BETWEEN breakpoints (content doesn't jump at neat 768px intervals), and watch tap targets (≥44px), text zoom (em/rem), and touch-vs-hover (hover: hover guards hover-styles from touch devices that emulate it stickily). The 'responsive' failure modes worth naming: horizontal scrollbars from a single unbreakable element (a wide image/table — fix with max-width: 100%, overflow-x: auto, or a table-wrap strategy).
